requirements.sourceBehavior: A readonly subagent cannot edit files or run state-changing shell commands, and may run shell commands that change nothing (Cursor subagents docs)
requirements.evidence: Cursor docs: readonly = "no file edits, no state-changing shell commands"; Cursor sandboxes shell with Seatbelt/Landlock, network blocked by default (cursor-docs-quotes.md). Pi implementation after reviews/resume-security.md findings: per-command sandbox policy (a shared pre-initialized permissive policy does not weaken it), dependency default writable paths (/tmp/claude, ~/.npm/_logs, ~/.claude/debug) denied, inherited BASH_ENV/ENV/BASH_FUNC_* stripped before the outer shell, pre-aborted calls never spawn, lifecycle (timeout, process-tree kill) delegated to Pi local operations (test/readonly-shell-security.test.ts through the real sandbox; test/e2e/task.e2e.test.ts through real Pi children). macOS verified. Observed Cursor deviations from its own docs: in the desktop Agents Window and the CLI, a Task call with readonly: true ran touch probe.txt with exit 0 (fixtures/0.15.21/user-captures/agents-window-task-readonly-touch-succeeds.jpg, cli-task-readonly-ignored-touch-succeeds.jpg; the Task schema lists no readonly field). Under a readonly agent file, the CLI blocked every shell call, including git log (evidence/cursor-readonly-v21-frontmatter-run1.json). Neither matches the documented contract, and both are recorded in decisions.md D14 as source defects the port does not reproduce.
requirements.piMapping: readonly children get bash backed by src/readonly-shell.ts: createBashTool with BashOperations that wrap each command in @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime with allowWrite [] and no network; fails closed where no sandbox can start
